# Cully v0.7.0

Cully's Codex advisor now has a compact full-width status pane with two prioritized comments, clear suggestion/tip counts and an expandable interactive advisor. Click the pane or press Ctrl+] / F6 to open it, select advice with the mouse or arrow keys, and press Enter to preview and accept an action. Tab opens the complete session instruments. The expanded advisor overlays the conversation without resizing the coding session.

Next, Watch, Warn, Tip and Apply labels separate workflow guidance from configuration changes. Supported shared project instruction/skill changes show exact contents before application and preserve existing user files. Task actions, commands and integration changes add a request to the current coding input for review and submission, preserving its draft. Informational tips have no Apply action.

The shared advisor works through Claude, Codex and Cursor adapters. It recalls owner/project-scoped Cully memory and performs targeted public research only for an evidenced capability gap. The foreground agent owns durable memory writes. Worker startup failures now distinguish memory not run from a failed recall, and command suggestions use the execution host's OS/shell and detected terminal metadata.

The status pane retains native model, context, token, quota and fast-mode information, Git changes, verification and tool counters. A red Messy phase flags observed failure density or repeated failures with unverified edits; high activity alone does not trigger it. Terminal background, wrapping and group spacing adapt to the available room.

Exiting or losing the terminal stops the wrapper's Codex process group and releases its session, including descendants that retain the PTY. No detached tmux session is created.

Validation: Go formatting, vet, full race tests and real PTY regression tests for input preservation, mouse/keyboard controls, handoff acceptance and process cleanup. Release automation publishes CLI/service binaries and service images. Personal deployment remains manual.

Every PR now has a changelog-update requirement in the repository instructions, PR checklist and CI. `CHANGELOG.md` keeps an Unreleased section for upcoming changes and versioned sections for published releases.
